messages.author: 71335e4c86a7e748
messages.subject: tidyr and reshape2
parts: Thanks for another great package Hadley! How do you see the future relationship between reshape2 and tidyr? Tidyr replacing reshape2 as the latter did with reshape or the two of them living along?

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: tidyr and reshape2
parts:
Basically you use tidyr to do data tidying, then dplyr for everything
else. Reshape2 does both tidying and (some types of) data munging.

Hadley

messages.author: c57d665324d4950a
messages.subject: Re: tidyr and reshape2
parts:
I've spent some time trying to use dplyr instead of reshape2 cast functions.  I am unable to match the ease of the dcast function for widening data frames using summarise/mutate in dplyr.    It seems the only way to get dplyr to cast is a combination of summarise, mutate, filter, and joins.    The window functions are great (but not enough it seems) -- maybe I'm just not sophisticated enough in my thinking to assemble dplyr recipes to accomplish the task. 

Would love to understand how you use dplyr to replicate cast functions.  Rather than solving a specific problem I have currently -- I'd like to better understand the "way" I should be thinking about these categories of problems.

Also -- I'd be happy to help/volunteer to aggregate common data needs and corresponding tidy+dplyr patterns.  Would love a resource for data manipulation patterns that is browseable and searchable beyond google groups/SO, etc.

Thanks,
John

messages.subject: Re: tidyr and reshape2
parts:
I need to carve out some time to share some replicable examples -- but spread doesn't work consistently (session terminations).  I've stuck with reshape2 and cast because it is fast and reliable.

I read the Tidy Data paper and want to employ the philosophy in everything I and my team does.  The Case Study in the paper uses plyr -- but also transform, subset, and join -- which dplyr can do.  I guess part of my interest is philosophical in that it seems "cast" and "spread" aren't "tidy" methods. 

I'll try to add specific examples to help.
